- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — leading to overshoot; cap upward revisions after strong price moves.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day average is rising, forecast should be slightly above that trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- In cases where true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% over 3–5 days, model is underestimating volatility — increase forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, model often fails to recognize downward bias — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
- Model tends to overcorrect after sharp declines — if true outcome rebounds sharply, forecast should be conservative for 2–3 days to avoid overbought signals.
